exposure: USG-guided TAP block with 0.2% ropivacaine alone
USG-guided TAP block with 0.2% ropivacaine and 4mg dexamethasone
outcome: Complications (intravascular injection, local anaesthesia systemic toxicity, haematoma at injection site, paresthesia, nausea, vomiting, hypotension, bradycardia)
cohort: Sixty pregnant patients classified as ASA-2, undergoing lower segment caesarean section (LSCS) under spinal anaesthesia.
finding: The addition of dexamethasone to ropivacaine in a USG-guided TAP block for LSCS significantly prolonged the time to first rescue analgesia from 15.21 hours to 22.82 hours.
followup_time: Up to 22.82 +/- 4.75 hours (time to first rescue analgesia)
